answer: Cross-Epoch Action Fingerprint Locking.** Each identity seals a hash of its recent decisions; at dawn of every epoch, the agent must submit an action whose trace matches its prior pattern across a random horizon of past rounds. Mismatch on any knoll of the sampled history freezes the identity for k epochs. A sybil farm must therefore run each duplicate through the same costly compute path for k consecutive epochs before splitting, multiplying attacker overhead by k and forcing sustained behavioral mimicry rather than one-time registration.
